# Shell Plugin — Mental Model

Shell = header bar + toolbar content + tool panels. Lives entirely in [plugins/shell/](libs/grid/src/lib/plugins/shell/) (`ShellPlugin.ts`, `shell.ts`, `shell-controller.ts`, `types.ts`). Shell builders still live in core `dom-builder.ts`.

**v3: shell is OPT-IN.** A bare `<tbw-grid>` renders NO shell chrome. Activate via `features: { shell: <ShellConfig|true> }` or `plugins: [new ShellPlugin(cfg)]`. Core has ZERO shell value-references.

- HARD RULE (#370): core MUST NOT reference any plugin. Enforced by `no-restricted-imports` in [eslint.config.mjs](eslint.config.mjs) scoped to `libs/grid/src/lib/core/**/*.ts` (ignores `*.spec.ts`), forbidding VALUE imports matching `**/plugins/shell{,/**}` with `allowTypeImports: true`. There is NO sanctioned core→shell value import.

## api & removals (#370 v3)

- Public API is ONLY `grid.getPluginByName('shell').<method>` (typed via `PluginNameMap['shell']`). The 15 `@deprecated` grid-element delegates (`open`/`close`/`toggleToolPanel`, `toggleToolPanelSection`, `get`/`register`/`unregisterToolPanel`, `get`/`register`/`unregister{HeaderContent,ToolbarContent}`, `isToolPanelOpen`, `expandedToolPanelSections`), `#warnShellApiDeprecated` and `TBW076 SHELL_API_DEPRECATED` are DELETED. `refreshShellHeader()` is KEPT on the grid element (`@internal` bridge for shell-controller + the Angular adapter).
- Auto-register is REMOVED: no `#shellPlugin` field, no `#resolveShellPlugin()`, no `TEMP-BUDGET-370`/`TEMP-SHELL-IMPORT`/`SHELL-AUTOREGISTER-V3-370` markers. Shell self-inits in `ShellPlugin.ensureState(grid)` on attach. `index.js` 145 kB raw / 42.46 kB gz; shell chunk 40.72 kB / 10.99 gz.
- Spec migration pattern: top-level `shell:` config → `features: { shell }`; register panels AFTER `await waitUpgrade(grid)` via `const shell = grid.getPluginByName('shell')` (the instance does not exist pre-connect).
- HISTORICAL LESSON (applies to any future delegate deprecation): before warning on a public delegate that first-party code also calls, REPOINT internal callers to the plugin instance first — otherwise the lib warns about itself.

## ownership-inversion hooks

- `processConfig(config)` (called by `ConfigManager.merge()`): ShellPlugin folds its OWN `shellState` (light-DOM title/content, API panels) + `this.resolvedConfig` (ctor/feature config, as BASE layer) into `config.shell`. Precedence: light-DOM/API state > top-level `gridConfig.shell` > feature/ctor. Core config holds ZERO shell knowledge.
- `afterStructuralRender()` (end of core `#render()`): ShellPlugin WRAPS `.tbw-shell-body` around the existing `.tbw-grid-content` via `rebuildShellDOM` (moving the node preserves listeners + cached refs `_bodyEl`/`_headerRowEl`/`__rowsBodyEl`). Core `#render()` always passes `shellConfig = undefined` to `buildBareGridDOMIntoElement`. State torn down on disconnect via `disposeShellState()`.
- FEATURE module `features/shell.ts`: `registerFeature('shell', cfg => new ShellPlugin(typeof cfg === 'boolean' ? {} : (cfg ?? {})))` + augments `FeatureConfig.shell?: boolean | ShellConfig`. Resolves via the existing `./features/*` wildcard (no new entry). `#render()` RE-MERGES after `#initializePlugins()` so `processConfig` runs before `afterStructuralRender` reads `effectiveConfig.shell`.

## resolution & instance identity

- DECIDED (#374): core MUST resolve shell via `#pluginManager.getPluginByName('shell')`, NOT `getPlugin(ShellPlugin)`. WHY: `pluginMap` is keyed by `plugin.constructor`, and in the DIST build core's `index.js` bundles its OWN ShellPlugin copy while `lib/plugins/shell/index.js` is a SEPARATE copy → two class identities → constructor lookup misses the feature-attached instance → `ensureState` never runs → `hasState === false` → no chrome (e2e: `.tbw-shell-title` absent in all 4 demos, passes in vitest). INVARIANT: any core→plugin instance lookup that must survive dist chunk duplication MUST use `getPluginByName`. Regression test: `features/shell.spec.ts` "renders the shell when the attached plugin class differs from core" (uses a `class extends ShellPlugin` subclass).
- DECIDED (#370, FEATURE-INSTANCE-GATE): a feature is instantiated at most once per grid. `#initializePlugins` routes every feature-resolved plugin through `#gateFeatureInstance(fresh)`, backed by `#featureInstances: Map<name, BaseGridPlugin>`. If an instance for `fresh.name` exists, REUSE it (`cached.refreshUserConfigFrom(fresh)`) and discard the fresh one. WHY: the factory builds a NEW instance with its OWN `#state` on every re-resolution — the SSR/docs pattern (connect from server HTML → auto-shell instance A → `registerToolPanel` writes onto A → `gridConfig.features.shell` assigned → re-resolve → instance B with EMPTY state → A detached) LOST all panels. `refreshUserConfigFrom(other)` = last-write-wins config replace (clear + `Object.assign` userConfig; `attach()` recomputes `config`) — distinct from `mergeConfigsFrom` (alias-collapse, conflict-throwing). INVARIANT: a feature plugin keeps its identity and accumulated state for the grid's lifetime.
- INVARIANT (#370 v3, empty-shell bootstrap): an empty `features: { shell: true }` renders no chrome, so the controller stays `initialized = false`. The 4 register methods in [shell-controller.ts](libs/grid/src/lib/plugins/shell/shell-controller.ts) MUST bootstrap chrome when connected-but-not-initialized: `if (initialized || grid._hostElement.isConnected)` → `grid.refreshShellHeader?.()` (header-content keeps the lightweight `renderHeaderContent` path only when ALREADY initialized). Use `grid._hostElement.isConnected`, NOT `grid.isConnected` (TS2339 at build). `initialState`/`defaultOpen`/`locked` all re-apply on post-upgrade registration.

## plugin dependencies on shell

| Plugin     | Declaration                                                                 | Effect                        |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Visibility | `{name:'shell',required:true}` (+ `{name:'reorder',required:false}`)        | THROWS TBW020 without shell   |
| Pivot      | `{name:'shell',required:false,severity:'warn',when:cfg=>cfg.showToolPanel}` | WARNS TBW021 when panel is on |
| Print      | none                                                                        | —                             |

Validated by `validatePluginDependencies`. Tests: `validate-config.spec.ts` "shell dependencies (#370)", `visibility-plugin.spec.ts`.

## light-DOM decoupling

- The THREE `registerLightDomHandler('tbw-grid-header'|'tbw-grid-tool-buttons'|'tbw-grid-tool-panel', …)` + `handleShellChange` live in ShellPlugin `attach()`; `unregisterLightDomHandler` in `detach()`. Core keeps ONLY `tbw-grid-column`/`tbw-grid-detail` + generic `observeLightDOM(this)`. `MutationObserver` infra stays tag-agnostic in `ConfigManager`.
- INVARIANT: no shell plugin ⇒ no handler ⇒ `<tbw-grid-header>` yields zero callbacks and zero config change. Unclaimed light-DOM config elements stay VISIBLE (the `headerEl.style.display='none'` hide is a ShellPlugin side effect) — an intended "you forgot the import" signal. MUST NOT add a core CSS rule hiding plugin-owned tags.
- EXCEPTION (Jul 2026): CORE-owned config tags that core ALWAYS consumes — `tbw-grid-column` and `tbw-grid-type` — ARE hidden by `base.css` (`tbw-grid > tbw-grid-column, tbw-grid > tbw-grid-type { display:none }`). WHY: they carry inline `<tbw-grid-column-view>`/`<tbw-grid-column-editor>` `{{ }}` templates that would otherwise render as raw markup above the grid; there is no "forgot to import" scenario. Hiding does not affect parsing or adapter template registration.
- DECIDED (id collisions): API registration > plugin > light-DOM. `TBW073`/`TBW074` warn on each override. Order-independent — enforced on both sides: `#collectPluginShellContributions` (grid.ts) overrides+cleans+warns unless the id ∈ `apiToolPanelIds`/`apiHeaderContentIds`; `parseLightDomToolPanels` (shell.ts) skips+hides+warns when the id ∈ `toolPanels` but ∉ `lightDomToolPanelIds`.
- DECIDED (adapter re-parse safety): `parseLightDomToolPanels` MUST NOT tear down adapter-rendered panel content on idempotent re-parses. Re-parse of an adapter-bound panel only refreshes the `render` closure + attributes; `panelCleanups` run only on (a) first adapter attach or (b) header attr change (order/icon/tooltip). WHY: every `grid.gridConfig = …` routes through `#applyGridConfigUpdate` → `parseLightDomToolPanels`; unconditional cleanup destroyed local state + `scrollTop`. Tracker: `ShellState.adapterBoundToolPanelIds`. Test: `shell.spec.ts` "does not tear down adapter-rendered panel content on idempotent re-parse".

## type ownership

- Canonical in [plugins/shell/types.ts](libs/grid/src/lib/plugins/shell/types.ts): `ShellConfig`, `ShellHeaderConfig`, `ToolPanelConfig`, `ToolbarContentDefinition`, `ToolPanelDefinition`, `HeaderContentDefinition`. The 6 `@deprecated` re-aliases are DELETED from `core/types.ts` and `public.ts` — they export ONLY from `@toolbox-web/grid/plugins/shell`.
- Core modules `import type { X } from '../plugins/shell/types'` (grid.ts, core/plugin/types.ts, base-plugin.ts, VisibilityPlugin, PivotPlugin, PrintPlugin). `GridConfig.shell` exists only via the plugin's `declare module '../../core/types'` augmentation (NON-deprecated — the supported config path). `ShellState` lives in `plugins/shell/shell.ts`; core imports it `import type`.
- ADAPTERS MUST import `HeaderContentDefinition`/`ToolbarContentDefinition`/`ShellConfig` from `@toolbox-web/grid/plugins/shell`, never the package root.

## CSS ownership split (CORRECTED)

- BOTH `.tbw-scroll-area` AND `.tbw-grid-content` are CORE layout and live in `core/styles/base.css`. `buildGridDOM` builds a `.tbw-grid-content` wrapper for EVERY grid; `rebuildShellDOM` WRAPS `.tbw-shell-body` around that SAME pre-existing node (it does not create it).
- INVARIANT: a CSS rule for DOM the core dom-builder ALWAYS renders MUST live in `base.css`, NEVER in a plugin stylesheet — plugin CSS only loads when the plugin is registered, and shell is opt-in at v3 (#260/#261/#262). RULED OUT: `.tbw-grid-content { flex:1; display:flex; min-height:0 }` in `shell.css` — collapsed the scroll-area to 37 px in every shell-less grid (all docs demos).
- `shell.css` owns only `.tbw-shell-*`, `.tbw-toolbar-*`, `.tbw-tool-panel*`, `.tbw-accordion*`.

## config behavior

- DECIDED (May 2026): `shell.header.toolPanelToggle: false` opts out of the built-in `<button.tbw-toolbar-btn[data-panel-toggle]>` AND the auto-inserted `.tbw-toolbar-separator`; panels stay registered/openable via the controller API. Gated in BOTH render paths — `renderShellHeader` (shell.ts) and `buildShellHeader` (dom-builder.ts, via `ShellHeaderOptions.showToggle`). Default `true`.
- DECIDED (#338): `shell.header.visible: false` suppresses the ENTIRE `.tbw-shell-header` bar while keeping tool panels mounted and openable. KEY INVARIANT: `shouldRenderShellHeader(config)` gates shell EXISTENCE (header bar + body); a SEPARATE `shouldRenderHeaderBar(config)` (`config?.header?.visible !== false`) gates ONLY the bar. Do NOT collapse them — the former returning false would also drop the panel-hosting `.tbw-shell-body`. Close affordances when the bar is hidden: (1) the `✕` button (`showCloseButton`), wired `[data-panel-close]` → `onPanelClose` → `closeToolPanel()`; (2) `setupEscapeDismiss` — Esc closes OVERLAY panels only (push is a persistent sidebar), always-on, yields on `e.defaultPrevented`; (3) `setupClickOutsideDismiss` — document-level `mousedown` gated by `closeOnClickOutside`, no-op in push mode. INVARIANT: shadow DOM retargets `event.target`, so click-outside MUST iterate `event.composedPath()`.
- DECIDED (May 2026, open state): three knobs on `shell.toolPanel`. `initialState: 'open'|'closed'` (default `'closed'`) is the forward-compatible control. `locked: true` implies open, makes `closeToolPanel()` a no-op, and suppresses the built-in toggle (folded into `showToggle`). `defaultOpen: '<id>'` selects which accordion section auto-expands on first open. TENSION: in v2.x `defaultOpen` ALSO opens the sidebar; v3.0.0 drops that (#259). The legacy fallback is gated by `initialState === undefined`, so `initialState: 'closed'` opts into v3 behavior today. Search marker `TOOLPANEL-OPEN-LEGACY-259` in grid.ts (`afterConnect` + `#afterShellRefresh`).
- INVARIANT (`#applyGridConfigUpdate` `needsFullRerender`, grid.ts): a `gridConfig` re-assignment changing ONLY `shell.toolPanel.mode` (`overlay`↔`push`↔`dropdown`) MUST be in the `needsFullRerender` set. The in-place path `#updateShellHeaderInPlace` only rewrites the header title — never `data-mode` on `.tbw-shell-body` nor the `popover` attribute — so a mode-only change otherwise left the DOM stuck. Read `prevMode` from `.tbw-shell-body` `dataset.mode` BEFORE merge and OR `(hadToolPanel && prevMode !== newMode)` in. Test: `grid.integration.spec.ts > updates the shell body data-mode when only toolPanel.mode changes`.
- DECIDED (close-button placement): `buildShellOptions` sets `showCloseButton` ONLY when `header.visible === false` AND `toolPanel.locked !== true` AND `mode !== 'dropdown'` (dropdown always light-dismisses; a locked panel can't close). PLACEMENT in `buildShellBody`: single panel ⇒ ✕ is a SIBLING of the accordion header `<button>` inside a flex `.tbw-accordion-header-row` (`.tbw-tool-panel-close--inline`); multi-panel ⇒ ✕ gets its own `.tbw-tool-panel-header` row. The accordion header IS a `<button>`, so the ✕ MUST NOT nest inside it. `renderShellBody` (string renderer) NEVER emits a close button — it is test-only/legacy.
- DECIDED (`ToolPanelDefinition.title` OPTIONAL, @since 3.1.0): accordion-header render rule in BOTH `buildShellBody` and `renderShellBody` is `renderHeader = !!panel.title || !isSinglePanel`. A SINGLE title-less panel skips the header (content shows directly; the section still gets `expanded` on open). Multiple panels keep the header with an empty `.tbw-accordion-title` spacer + chevron so the toggle stays available. When a single title-less panel needs an inline close, the ✕ falls back to a standalone `.tbw-tool-panel-header` row. INVARIANT: `renderShellBody` MUST wrap the title in `escapeHtml(panel.title ?? '')` (XSS sink — titles come from user config/light DOM); the DOM path uses `textContent`.

## dropdown mode (#375)

Third `toolPanel.mode` beside `'overlay'`/`'push'` — the whole sidebar as an anchored popover.

- IMPL: dom-builder/`renderShellBody` add `popover="manual"` to `.tbw-tool-panel` in dropdown mode ONLY (`manual`, NOT `auto` — platform light-dismiss would race a consumer toggle button). Show/hide via `showToolPanelDropdown`/`hideToolPanelDropdown` (shell.ts) called from the controller's `openToolPanel`/`closeToolPanel`. Positioning: CSS anchor positioning (`anchor-name`/`position-anchor`/`position-try-fallbacks`) behind `@supports (anchor-name: --x)`, else JS `positionDropdownFallback` (fixed coords from `getBoundingClientRect`).
- Anchor priority: explicit `OpenToolPanelOptions.anchor` (@since 2.16.0) → `[data-panel-toggle]` → grid corner (`grid._hostElement`, sets `data-anchor='corner'`). `state.dropdownAnchorEl` tracks it so `setupClickOutsideDismiss` ignores clicks on it. Dropdown ALWAYS light-dismisses regardless of `closeOnClickOutside`. Resize handle hidden; popover capped `max-height: min(70vh, 480px)`.
- All Popover/anchor calls are guarded (`typeof panel.showPopover === 'function'`, `CSS.supports`) — happy-dom lacks both, so tests assert attributes/`dataset.anchor`/state, not top-layer render.
- INVARIANT (CSS): dropdown CSS MUST re-assert `.tbw-tool-panel[popover] { display: none }` + open via `&:popover-open, &.open { display: flex }` — the base `.tbw-tool-panel { display: flex }` author rule (same `@layer tbw-base`) outranks the UA `[popover]:not(:popover-open){display:none}` origin and would leak the CLOSED popover over the header. The `&.open` arm is the no-Popover-API fallback (`updatePanelState` JS-toggles `.open` regardless of mode).
- INVARIANT (multi-grid): (a) `showToolPanelDropdown` mints a UNIQUE `anchor-name` per show (`--tbw-tool-panel-anchor-${++seq}`, stored in `state.dropdownAnchorName`) — a shared constant name pairs grid A's popover with grid B's trigger. (b) `setupClickOutsideDismiss` matches `.tbw-tool-panel`/`[data-panel-toggle]` ONLY via `isInGrid(node, gridElement)` (`contains` OR `getRootNode().host === gridElement`) — unscoped matching leaves grid A stuck open when grid B opens.

### re-anchoring after re-render (#378, #379)

- PROBLEM: `afterStructuralRender` → `rebuildShellDOM` rebuilds `.tbw-tool-panel` on EVERY structural render, so the fresh panel is not in the top layer and the anchored trigger may have been recreated by the same render. Without re-anchoring the popover loses its `position-anchor` and collapses to the viewport corner — looks closed, but `closeToolPanel`/`hidePopover` never fired.
- MECHANISM: while a dropdown is open, `ShellPlugin` runs a `MutationObserver` (`#reanchorObserver`, lazily started in `afterRender`, scoped to `grid._renderRoot`, `{childList:true,subtree:true}` — NOT attributes, so the re-pair's own style writes don't re-trigger it) calling `reanchorOpenDropdown()` on every mutation. Observer beats rAF: its callback is a PRE-PAINT microtask (no flash) and it is event-driven (never misses a late React commit). `afterRender` ALSO calls `reanchorOpenDropdown()` synchronously as a backstop (and is the only path in happy-dom/SSR). `#renderShellContents` calls it too inside `if (state.isPanelOpen)`, dropdown-mode only. Observer disconnected on panel close, grid disconnect (`disposeShellState`), and when state goes away.
- RE-PAIR IS IN-PLACE: `repairDropdownAnchor(renderRoot, state, trigger)` (shell.ts) MOVES the already-minted `anchor-name` onto the fresh `[data-panel-toggle]` and clears stale `top`/`left`/`right` WITHOUT re-entering the Popover API (a re-show mints a new name and flashes to corner). Gated by `supportsAnchorPositioning()` (exported); when unsupported, falls back to `showToolPanelDropdown(fresh, false)`. `reanchorOpenDropdown` keeps an idempotent fast path (no-op when the stored trigger is connected AND still carries `state.dropdownAnchorName`).
- No live trigger: a corner-origin dropdown (stored anchor === grid host) stays pinned to the corner; a trigger-origin dropdown whose trigger is TRANSIENTLY absent is LEFT AT ITS LAST POSITION (no corner flash) — the observer re-pairs it before paint once the framework re-commits.
- INVARIANT: a consumer's custom dropdown trigger MUST carry `data-panel-toggle` to survive node recreation — an explicit `OpenToolPanelOptions.anchor` ref alone is lost once the host re-renders it.
- #379 hardening: (1) `#startReanchorObserver` calls `#stopReanchorObserver()` before its early return when mode is no longer `'dropdown'` (else it watched `_renderRoot` forever). (2) `repairDropdownAnchor` idempotently calls `panel.showPopover()` (try/catch) after rewiring `position-anchor` — a rebuilt panel is not in the top layer. (3) The fallback-mode fast path (no `dropdownAnchorName`) short-circuits ONLY when the current panel already has `dataset.anchor === 'below'`, so a freshly rebuilt panel never wrongly skips the re-show.
- Tests: `shell.spec.ts` (repairDropdownAnchor / reanchorOpenDropdown suites), `ShellPlugin.spec.ts` (observer lifecycle), `grid.integration.spec.ts` (popover open/close + anchor resolution), `dom-builder.spec.ts`. Demo: `apps/docs/.../demos/shell/ShellDropdownDemo.astro`.
